call_points.text: July was the best of the four months this year and volume picked up after the MIP, but management declined to quantify it.
Cash stands at ₹2,636 Cr; any large deployment or return to shareholders is for the Board to decide.
Capital outlay remains in the ₹125-200 Cr range, with capacity added through debottlenecking rather than a large greenfield or brownfield project.
VCM availability remains limited by Middle East force majeure and logistics; the Ratnagiri jetty cannot import VCM during the four monsoon months.
Management declined to give month-wise volume figures for April-June, saying the data was not immediately available.
Q4 included a ₹35-40 Cr inventory gain from the March PVC price spike.
Annual maintenance capex of roughly ₹100-odd crores, with debottlenecking ongoing.
Net free cash of about ₹2,563 Cr; board has not decided on deploying the surplus.
Middle East conflict disrupting VCM supply; company is shifting sourcing to Far East and Northeast Asia.
April demand was subdued after the March price spike; May showed some improvement.

operating_notes.text: Q4 PVC/EDC spread averaged $521 with PVC prices at $793; currently spread is $543 with prices around $900-plus.
PVC/VCM spread narrowed to $108 currently from a Q4 average of $179-180.
CPVC share of volume was 7-8% in Q4FY26 versus 6-7% a year ago; fittings share was 9% in Q4 and 11% for the full year.
Q1FY27 PVC averaged USD 863/t with a PVC-EDC spread of USD 501/t, versus USD 698/t and USD 522/t a year ago.
Installed capacity is 520 (MT) against FY26 volume of 333, giving headroom to grow 10-12% for the next 1-1.5 years.
JJM 2.0 allocation is about ₹67,000 Cr, lower than JJM 1.0, with sales routed through channel partners.

timeline.summary: On 27 May 2026, Finolex Industries held its Q4 FY26 earnings call, guiding FY27 EBITDA margin below 15% and volume growth in high single to low double digits.
On its 7 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, Finolex reported a 27% YoY volume fall to about 68,000 MT and 15% lower revenue of ₹884 Cr, while EBITDA rose 14% to ₹107 Cr and margin improved to 12%.
